newsitem.title: ITALY: Marzotto sees lower 1996 profits - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Marzotto sees lower 1996 profits - analysts.

text.p: Italian clothing and textiles group Marzotto SpA, which controls German company Hugo Boss, expects to post 1996 net profit of between 40-50 billion lire against 50 billion lire group net in 1995.
But it sees full year net debt lower at 500 billion lire against 550 billion and aims to divest certain non-core businesses, starting perhaps before end-1996.
These were the main points emerging from a meeting with analysts last Friday.
Analysts said Marzotto confirmed its expectations of a 1996 turnover around 2.20 trillion lire against 2.36 trillion lire in 1995.

But the group said signals from the Italian market were fairly gloomy, with orders for its spring-summer 1997 collection down some eight to 10 percent on 1996. However, forecasts were positive for 1998.
"Figures which came out of the meeting indicate a 1996 operating profit of around 190 billion lire, against 207.8 billion," said Elena Sottanella, analyst at Pasfin brokers.

"For 1997, I see the stock priced about right around 9,000 lire," said Luisa De Maria, analyst at Credit Sim brokers. "The problem is that its profit trend is tightly linked to the linen sector which is highly dependent on fashion whims and changes."
At 1335 GMT. Marzotto was quoted 53 lire down at a new 1996 low of 8,590 lire, after a year's high of 11,500 lire touched on March 1.

"The stock has lost a lot. At current levels it could be interesting," said one analyst who declined to be named. "For Hugo Boss, I see a phase of consolidation helped by the fact that in 1997 we are not likely to see a renewed strengthening of the lira."

Sottanella said, however, "I think that Marzotto's current share price has for the most part discounted the results expected for 1996. I don't think the stock is very interesting unless the first months of 1997 show better results than expected."

Marzotto posted first half 1996 consolidated net profit of 14.8 billion lire against a previous 20.4 billion profit with a consolidated operating profit of 91.2 billion lire, down 7.4 percent on the same 1995 period. Group turnover was 1.09 trillion lire against 1.16 trillion.
